title: Remove the Shortest Block to Make the Sum Divisible

concept.title: The remainder that has to disappear, and the nearest earlier prefix
body: The total sum has the remainder `r = total % p`. If `r = 0` nothing has to be removed. Otherwise you must remove a block whose sum has the **same remainder `r`** modulo `p`, because then the rest has remainder `0`. You want the **shortest** such block, and the block may not be the whole array.

A block ending at `j` has remainder `r` when `prefix[j] - prefix[i] ≡ r (mod p)`, i.e. `prefix[i] ≡ prefix[j] - r (mod p)`. To make the block short, `i` should be as **late** as possible: store the **last** position of every prefix remainder in a map.
Look the partner up **before** storing the current prefix. If the best block has the whole length `n`, it is not allowed, and the answer is -1.

statement: You are given `n` positive integers and a number `p`. You may remove one block of consecutive elements (also an empty block) so that the sum of the remaining elements is divisible by `p`. You may not remove all elements. Print the length of the shortest block that has to be removed, or -1 if it is impossible.
outputFormat: Print the length of the shortest block, or -1.

examples.note: The sum is 10, remainder 4. Removing the block 4 (one element) leaves 6.

hints: If the total is already divisible by p, remove nothing: print 0.
Otherwise look for a block whose sum has the same remainder `r` as the total.
Store the last position of every prefix remainder and look up `(cur - r) mod p` for each end.

explanation: The removed block must have the same remainder as the total sum. A map of the last position of every prefix remainder gives the shortest such block ending at each position.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, p = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

total = sum(a)
r = total % p
if r == 0:
    print(0)
else:
    last = {0: -1}
    cur = 0
    best = n
    for j in range(n):
        cur = (cur + a[j]) % p
        need = (cur - r) % p
        if need in last:
            best = min(best, j - last[need])
        last[cur] = j
    print(best if best < n else -1)
